01 - Exploratory data analysis: Decode the Bioreactor (Project 1 - DTB)¶

Goal of this notebook (no modelling yet):

  1. understand the file format, batches, sampling and missing values;
  2. work out how the feeds and reactor volume are encoded (needed for mass balances / dilution);
  3. identify the train / test split and the submission format;
  4. plot VCD, DCD, substrate and byproduct per batch with feed times, plus descriptive statistics.

Data are read straight from ~/work/input-data/Project 1 - DTB/ (read-only) via src/data.py.

1. Files and raw format¶

File Content
bioreaction_remaining.csv all batches, sparse event log (measurements + feed events + rows to predict)
bioreaction_template.csv submission template: batch_id, elapsed_time, vcd, tcd, substrate, byproduct (zeros)
Leaderboard_template.ipynb get_leaderboard() / submit(df, user="Team XX") against the organisers' API

No documentation of units is provided. Plausible (unconfirmed) units: time in days, VCD/TCD in 10⁶ cells/mL, substrate/byproduct in g/L (glucose/lactate-like ranges), volume in an unspecified unit (L or mL, ~10.5 → 16.5).

In [3]:
# Each row is exactly one kind of event: check it.
is_meas = raw[D.TARGETS].notna()
is_feed = raw[D.FEEDS].notna()
print("measurement rows with a partial set of targets:", ((is_meas.sum(axis=1) > 0) & (is_meas.sum(axis=1) < 4)).sum())
print("rows with a measurement AND a feed:", (is_meas.any(axis=1) & is_feed.any(axis=1)).sum())
print("feed rows with >1 feed column filled:", (is_feed.sum(axis=1) > 1).sum())
print("volume filled on:", raw.groupby("row_type")["volume"].apply(lambda s: f"{s.notna().mean():.0%}").to_dict())
print("TCD < VCD anywhere:", (raw["tcd"] < raw["vcd"]).sum(), "| negative values:", (raw[D.TARGETS + D.FEEDS] < 0).sum().sum())

measurement rows with a partial set of targets: 0
rows with a measurement AND a feed: 0
feed rows with >1 feed column filled: 0
volume filled on: {'feed': '0%', 'measurement': '100%', 'to_predict': '100%'}
TCD < VCD anywhere: 0 | negative values: 0

Missing values are structural, not random: a measurement row has all 4 targets + volume and no feed; a feed row has exactly one feed value and nothing else. There are no partial measurements, no negative values, and TCD ≥ VCD everywhere, so DCD = TCD − VCD is well defined.

Split imposed by the organisers: 12 test batches (Batch5, 6, 12, 24, 32, 35, 40, 48, 54, 56, 57, 60) have only the t = 0 measurement; their feed events and the reactor volume at each sampling time are given. The template asks for vcd, tcd, substrate and byproduct at their 13 later sampling times (156 rows, exactly the to_predict=True rows). This matches the evaluation rule: predict a run from initial conditions + feed profile only.

The leaderboard submit() returns metrics computed server-side (not documented in the template); it needs a team name "Team XX".

Sampling is daily and nearly regular (14 samples, day 0 to ~13; intervals 0.85-1.10 d, timestamps jitter by a few hours around the daily grid). Time stamps are not identical across batches, so models should work in continuous time (ODE / interpolation) rather than on a fixed index.

# Volume balance: between two samples, does measured delta V equal the sum of feed volumes?
vb = D.volume_balance(raw)
print(f"corr(delta V, sum of feeds) = {np.corrcoef(vb.dV, vb.fed)[0,1]:.4f}")
display(vb["removed"].describe().round(4).to_frame("removed = fed - dV").T)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.5))
ax[0].scatter(vb.fed, vb.dV, s=6, alpha=0.5)
lim = [vb.fed.min(), vb.fed.max()]; ax[0].plot(lim, lim, "k--", lw=1, label="dV = fed")
ax[0].set_xlabel("sum of feed volumes in interval"); ax[0].set_ylabel("measured delta V"); ax[0].legend()
ax[1].hist(vb.removed, bins=40); ax[1].set_xlabel("fed - delta V  (sampling / evaporation loss)")
plt.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / "volume_balance.png", bbox_inches="tight")

corr(delta V, sum of feeds) = 0.9974
count mean std min 25% 50% 75% max
removed = fed - dV 793.0 0.0334 0.0289 -0.0763 0.0186 0.0436 0.0532 0.0898

Feeds are instantaneous bolus additions of volume, expressed in the same unit as volume:

  • each feed value is the volume added at that time stamp (not cumulative, not a flow rate);
  • ΔV between samples = Σ feed volumes − ~0.04 (median), i.e. a small volume removal per sampling interval (sample withdrawal and/or evaporation), corr = 0.997;
  • the reactor volume is given at every sampling time, including the test rows to predict, so V(t) can be reconstructed exactly between samples (D.volume_profile) without modelling the losses.

For mass balances: a bolus of volume ΔV_f with concentration C_f gives V⁺ = V + ΔV_f and X⁺ = X·V/V⁺ (dilution), S⁺ = (S·V + C_f·ΔV_f)/V⁺. Feed concentrations are not given and must be estimated.

Feed B / (last VCD):  {'count': 588.0, 'mean': 0.0275, 'std': 0.006, 'min': 0.0142, '25%': 0.0232, '50%': 0.0279, '75%': 0.0316, 'max': 0.0418}
In [9]:
# Rough substrate mass balance over each sampling interval (training batches):
#   V2*S2 - V1*S1 = C_s * (substrate feed vol) + C_b * (Feed B vol) - qS * integral(Xv*V dt)
# Solving by linear least squares gives order-of-magnitude feed concentrations (exploratory only).
rows = []
for bid, g in tr.groupby("batch_id"):
    ms = g[g.row_type == "measurement"]
    for a, c in zip(ms.itertuples(), list(ms.itertuples())[1:]):
        w = g[(g.elapsed_time > a.elapsed_time) & (g.elapsed_time <= c.elapsed_time)]
        rows.append(dict(dS=c.volume * c.substrate - a.volume * a.substrate,
                         dP=c.volume * c.byproduct - a.volume * a.byproduct,
                         fs=w.feed_substrate.sum(), fb=w.feed_b.sum(), fc=w.feed_c.sum(), fd=w.feed_d.sum(),
                         XVdt=0.5 * (a.vcd * a.volume + c.vcd * c.volume) * (c.elapsed_time - a.elapsed_time)))
mb = pd.DataFrame(rows)
A = np.c_[mb.fs, mb.fb, -mb.XVdt]
coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, mb.dS, rcond=None)
r2 = 1 - ((mb.dS - A @ coef) ** 2).sum() / ((mb.dS - mb.dS.mean()) ** 2).sum()
print(f"C_substrate_feed ~ {coef[0]:.0f}, C_feedB ~ {coef[1]:.0f} (substrate units), mean qS ~ {coef[2]:.3f} /(cell unit*d); R2 = {r2:.2f}")

C_substrate_feed ~ 251, C_feedB ~ 52 (substrate units), mean qS ~ 0.110 /(cell unit*d); R2 = 0.68

Feeding strategy (from the training batches):

  • Feed B: main nutrient feed, 12 daily boluses (~day 1 → 12) just after sampling, total ≈ 6.6 volume units (≈ 60 % of the initial volume!), bolus size proportional to the last VCD (r ≈ 0.87). It clearly contains substrate (≈ 50 substrate units per volume unit from the balance above).
  • Substrate feed: concentrated substrate (~250 units / volume unit, ~5× Feed B), 1-3 small boluses late in the run (mostly ~day 11.5), triggered when the substrate falls below ≈ 1-2.
  • Feed C: tiny fixed-size boluses (≈ 0.00085 or 0.0018), 14-35 per batch starting day ~1.5-3.7: looks like an on-demand additive (e.g. base / antifoam); negligible volume.
  • Feed D: 3 boluses at fixed days 5, 8, 10 (≈ 0.011-0.017): a supplement with negligible volume whose effect, if any, will have to be learned.

⚠️ Because Feed B is sized from the measured VCD, the feed profile of a test batch carries information about its growth. Using it as an input is allowed (it's part of the given feed profile), but it should be kept in mind when interpreting the model (correlation ≠ causal feeding effect).

5. Time courses per batch (with feed times)¶

In [10]:
COLORS = {"feed_substrate": "tab:red", "feed_b": "tab:green", "feed_c": "0.7", "feed_d": "tab:purple"}
VAR_LABELS = {"vcd": "VCD", "dcd": "DCD = TCD-VCD", "substrate": "Substrate", "byproduct": "Byproduct"}

def plot_batch(bid, axes=None, feeds=("feed_substrate", "feed_b", "feed_d")):
    # 4 panels (VCD, DCD, substrate, byproduct) for one batch, feed times as vertical lines.
    mb = D.measurements(raw[raw.batch_id == bid])
    fb = D.feeds_long(raw[raw.batch_id == bid])
    if axes is None:
        _, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(16, 3))
    for ax, var in zip(axes, VAR_LABELS):
        ax.plot(mb.elapsed_time, mb[var], "o-", ms=3)
        for fn in feeds:
            for t in fb.loc[fb.feed == fn, "elapsed_time"]:
                ax.axvline(t, color=COLORS[fn], lw=0.8, alpha=0.6)
        ax.set_title(f"{bid} - {VAR_LABELS[var]}", fontsize=9)
    return axes

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 4, figsize=(16, 11), sharex=True)
for row, bid in zip(axes, ["Batch1", "Batch10", "Batch23", "Batch49"]):
    plot_batch(bid, row)
for fn in ["feed_b", "feed_substrate", "feed_d"]:
    axes[0, 0].plot([], [], color=COLORS[fn], label=D.FEED_LABELS[fn])
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=7)
for ax in axes[-1]: ax.set_xlabel("time [d]")
plt.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / "example_batches.png", bbox_inches="tight")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(7, 7, figsize=(18, 15), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    for ax, bid in zip(axes.flat, train_ids):
        g = mtr[mtr.batch_id == bid]
        ax.plot(g.elapsed_time, g[var], "o-", ms=2, lw=1)
        fb = ftr[ftr.batch_id == bid]

                      color=COLORS[fn], lw=0.8, alpha=0.5)
        ax.set_title(bid, fontsize=8, pad=2)

    axes[0].step(cf.index, cf["feed_b"], where="post", lw=1)

    axes[2].plot(vp.elapsed_time, vp.volume, lw=1, label=bid)

# Specific rates from finite differences (train), corrected for dilution by the measured volume.
# mu_app = d ln(Xv*V)/dt ; qS_app and qP_app use total amounts. Rough, but gives the phase structure.
rows = []
for bid, g in tr.groupby("batch_id"):
    ms = g[g.row_type == "measurement"].reset_index(drop=True)
    for i in range(1, len(ms)):
        a, c = ms.iloc[i - 1], ms.iloc[i]
        w = g[(g.elapsed_time > a.elapsed_time) & (g.elapsed_time <= c.elapsed_time)]
        dt_ = c.elapsed_time - a.elapsed_time
        XV = 0.5 * (a.vcd * a.volume + c.vcd * c.volume)
        rows.append(dict(batch_id=bid, t=0.5 * (a.elapsed_time + c.elapsed_time),
                         mu_app=np.log(c.vcd * c.volume / (a.vcd * a.volume)) / dt_,
                         qP_app=(c.volume * c.byproduct - a.volume * a.byproduct) / (XV * dt_),
                         S_mid=0.5 * (a.substrate + c.substrate), P_mid=0.5 * (a.byproduct + c.byproduct)))
rates = pd.DataFrame(rows)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 3.6))
for ax, (y, lab) in zip(axes[:2], [("mu_app", "apparent net growth rate [1/d]"), ("qP_app", "net specific byproduct rate")]):
    ax.scatter(rates.t, rates[y], s=5, alpha=0.4); ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.7); ax.set_title(lab); ax.set_xlabel("time [d]")
sc = axes[2].scatter(rates.S_mid, rates.mu_app, c=rates.t, s=6, cmap="viridis"); plt.colorbar(sc, ax=axes[2], label="t [d]")
axes[2].set_xlabel("substrate"); axes[2].set_ylabel("mu_app"); axes[2].set_title("growth rate vs substrate")
plt.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / "apparent_rates.png", bbox_inches="tight")

7. Observations¶

Data / setup

  • 61 batches × 14 daily samples (day 0 → ~12.9). 49 train batches, 12 test batches (only day 0 + feeds + volume given).
  • No random missing values; missingness is structural (event-log format). DCD = TCD − VCD ≥ 0.
  • Batches are very similar (same process recipe): initial VCD 1.08 ± 0.12, substrate 4.66 ± 0.13, V₀ 10.45 ± 0.08. Between-batch variability is mostly moderate; test batches lie inside the training envelope.

Dynamics

  • Growth: exponential phase days 0-5 (μ_app ≈ 0.7-0.8 /d), peak VCD ≈ 32 ± 3 around day 7-8, then decline (~22 at day 13). Peak VCD correlates with initial VCD (r ≈ 0.6).
  • μ falls steadily from day 2 while substrate stays ~2-3 → growth is not substrate-limited in the Monod sense (K_S must be small). The slowdown needs another mechanism: byproduct inhibition early, plus a density / time / unmeasured-nutrient limitation late (byproduct decreases after day 5 while μ keeps decreasing).
  • Death: DCD grows slowly then accelerates after day 10; viability 0.99 → 0.89. Suggests a death rate that increases late (e.g. with time, low substrate or accumulated stress), dead cells being diluted, little lysis.
  • Substrate: consumed from 4.7 to ~2 by day 4, then sustained by Feed B; jumps at day ~6 and a sharp drop at day ~11 (Feed B boluses become smaller after day 10), then rescued by the substrate feed.
  • Byproduct: produced fast in days 0-4 (q_P ≈ 0.45 → 0), peaks ≈ 2.5 at day 4-5, then consumed (metabolic shift) down to ~0.5. A plain Luedeking-Piret term (always ≥ 0) cannot do that: we need a consumption term (e.g. uptake when substrate/growth is low). Two batches show late re-accumulation (P_end ≈ 1.9).

Feeds / volume (key for mass balances)

  • Feeds = instantaneous bolus volumes; volume measured at every sample (test rows included) → dilution known.
  • Feed B ≈ 60 % of V₀ in total: dilution is a first-order effect and cannot be ignored.
  • Estimated substrate content: substrate feed ≈ 250, Feed B ≈ 50 (substrate units per volume unit). To be refined as model parameters. Feed C and D volumes are negligible; any effect is via composition (unknown).
  • Feed B size depends on measured VCD → feed profile partly encodes the batch's growth.
